basic_identification.full_title: Agro Textiles — Nylon Knitted Seamless Gloves for Tobacco Harvesters — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agro-tech (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the constructional details, dimensional parameters, mass, and performance-testing requirements (including skin safety, durability, and worker dexterity) for white knitted seamless gloves manufactured from high-quality nylon yarn. These gloves are designed specifically for workers engaged in cultivating and harvesting tobacco plants to protect them from skin contact irritation, mechanical cuts, and Green Tobacco Sickness (GTS) caused by transdermal nicotine absorption.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Agrotech Textiles / Worker Personal Protective Equipment)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Nylon Knitted Seamless Gloves for Tobacco Harvesters manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 16390:2015 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified protective gloves in the domestic market is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to protective textile gloves.

requirements.detail: Every pack or bundle of certified nylon harvester gloves must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 16390) printed on a secure label or packaging.
The gloves must be knitted from high-strength, non-toxic, and skin-friendly nylon yarn conforming to Table 1, ensuring maximum elasticity and resistance to mechanical abrasions.

requirements.requirement_type: Yarn Quality and Nips per Meter
requirements.detail: The nylon yarn used for knitting must be evaluated to ensure uniform structural behavior. The number of yarn nips per meter must be verified under twist-meter tension in accordance with the test procedures in Annex C.
The gloves must be constructed completely seamless without internal seams or ridges. This design prevents friction blisters, chafing, and hand fatigue during extended shifts in tobacco fields.

Standard length, width, and cuff parameters are checked correct to the nearest millimeter as per Annex D. The knitting density (measured as number of Wales and Courses per unit length) must be tightly controlled to prevent tobacco sap from penetrating the weave.

Finished gloves are weighed to ensure they meet specified nominal weights to guarantee appropriate fabric density. A strict tolerance of minus 5 percent is permissible on the mass of an individual glove pair calculated against standard nominal mass.

To prevent shrinkage or bagging during exposure to rain or soil moisture, glove specimens are relaxed by soaking flat under a head of 25 mm of water containing a 0.5% wetting agent for 2 hours, then dried at room temperature per Clause D-6.2. The maximum dimensional change (shrinkage or stretch) due to relaxation is strictly limited to 2.5 percent.

requirements.requirement_type: Dermatological pH Balance of Aqueous Extract
requirements.detail: To prevent chemical skin irritation, contact dermatitis, and rashes during prolonged, sweaty wear, the pH of the cold aqueous extract of the glove must lie strictly within the range of 5.0 to 7.5 when tested per IS 1390.

requirements.requirement_type: Processing Oil and Scouring Loss Limits
requirements.detail: To eliminate chemical lubricants, spin finishes, or knitting oils that could trigger allergic skin reactions, the finished gloves must satisfy strict minimum scouring loss limits evaluated as per Annex D.
The glove faces must withstand continuous frictional contact with rough tobacco leaves, demonstrating high abrasion resistance and maintaining specified yarn strength after wear cycles.
To ensure maximum comfort under tropical agricultural climates and prevent excessive sweating, the glove fabric must achieve high moisture vapor transmission rates.

requirements.requirement_type: Mandatory Glove Finger Dexterity (Table 4 & Clause D-8)
requirements.detail: To ensure workers maintain necessary tactile sensitivity, a trained operator wearing the gloves must successfully pick up a solid, centreless ground stainless steel test pin (40 mm long, 11 mm diameter) by its circumference between the glove's forefinger and thumb 3 consecutive times without fumbling, within a maximum limit of 30 seconds for all four gloves tested.

Characteristics that cannot be evaluated mathematically (including general appearance, lustre, tactile feel, and surface finish) must conform to a physical sealed sample agreed upon between the buyer and the seller.

Random samples are drawn as per Table 5 for visual/dimensional (non-destructive) and mechanical/chemical (destructive) testing to determine lot compliance. Non-conforming defectives must not exceed the specified Acceptance numbers for each lot size variety.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16390 : 2015 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification regulating white, seamless, nylon knitted protective gloves worn by agricultural workers harvesting tobacco. Under the statutory national Agro Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all such harvester gloves supplied to the Indian market must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Tobacco harvesting involves direct exposure to wet leaves covered in nicotine and crop chemicals, which can cause Green Tobacco Sickness (GTS) and skin irritation through dermal absorption. This standard protects workers by enforcing strict physical, chemical, and mechanical requirements—including high-quality non-toxic nylon yarn, seamless construction to prevent blisters, a maximum dimensional relaxation change of 2.5% to prevent loose fit, a skin-neutral pH range of 5.0 to 7.5, and low scouring loss to remove processing oil residues. It also mandates a precise tactile dexterity test (using an 11 mm steel test pin) to ensure workers maintain high finger sensitivity while handling crops.
